examples.title: Squat jump: stand, squat, jump, land
examples.tagline: Rewarded for the action, not for copying the clip: the Tracking, Task and Task (no reference) policies completed every stage (9/9) with 0 falls; the task policies did it 0.4–1.1 m (mean torso distance) away from the clip's own path.

examples.title: Squat: three rewards, one skill
examples.tagline: Shown one phone video of two squats, three policies trained with different rewards all complete it (5/5 stages, no falls), though their V-JEPA 2 similarity to the clip ranges from 0.53 to 0.71.

examples.title: A human body on G1 proportions
examples.tagline: Rebuilding the person on the G1's own bone lengths keeps their joint angles (2.4–10× smaller angle error) and plants the feet: foot sliding drops from 29.1 to 0.4 cm/s, averaged over 7 clips.

examples.title: Imitate what serves the jump
examples.tagline: Arm-waving added before the jump gets the minimum weight (0.10, the same as standing still) while the takeoff push and the landing peak at 0.97–1.00.

examples.title: Pushed, tripped, re-weighted
examples.tagline: 64 simulated rollouts per condition: the squat policies barely notice friction and mass changes, and tracking is the sturdiest under shoves and noisy starts. Latent falls most, which is why the task reward only pays while the robot stays upright.
